transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-30
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Zenith Head of Data), Tom Reed (Zenith Security Architect), Sara Liu (Zenith PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Discussed POC scope focused on data handling and privacy controls during pilot.
- Agreement on 2-week pilot with benchmarks: p50/p95 latency targets, throughput (rps), and quality checks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, with Diego on the SE side. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Aisha: Good, thanks. Busy quarter but excited to move on this.
[00:10] Diego: Quick agenda — we want to scope the POC: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and specifically data handling concerns, right?
[00:16] Sara: Yeah, primary ask from product is we need to be sure PII is never persisted beyond what we agree and that logs are redacted.
[00:22] Tom: And on the security side, we need clear answers on KMS, audit logs, and retention settings, plus whether prompts are stored in plain text.
[00:30] Maya: Totally, that's in scope. My high-level proposal is a two week pilot: week one for integration and baseline benchmarks, week two for workload runs and acceptance tests.
[00:38] Aisha: Sounds good. For sizing — traffic during the pilot is modest: around 50 rps peak, sustained 10-15 rps, but we want to validate a production projection of 200 rps later.
[00:48] Diego: Okay that maps. For latency targets what are you thinking — 200ms p50 and sub 800ms p95 for short prompts?
[00:56] Sara: 200/800 sounds fine as long as we understand how tokenization will affect longer prompts.
[01:03] Tom: Also, we need to know where the prompts are stored. We can't have raw PHI sitting in vendor logs. Can you walk through Redwood's logging and retention model?
[01:12] Maya: Sure — by default hosted endpoints log requests for a short period for debugging, but we have retention settings and an option to disable persistent storage. We also offer an enterprise private mode where you can opt out of any persistent prompt retention entirely; Diego can add details.
[01:25] Diego: Right. For the POC we can configure: (1) no persistent prompt storage, (2) redact PII client-side or server-side using configurable regex/de-identification rules, and (3) send logs to your syslog/Kafka via our connector so you control retention. Caveat: server-side redaction is heuristic — we recommend client-side tokenization for PHI-heavy payloads.
[01:45] Aisha: Heuristic redaction worries me. We have a set of regulated identifiers that must be removed. Does Redwood support custom redaction rules and a pre-processing hook?
[01:53] Diego: Yes — you can supply custom redaction patterns and we have an API to pre-process prompts. For sensitive workloads we commonly require a small filter step on the customer side to strip PHI before hitting our endpoints.
[02:05] Tom: KMS integration? We need envelope encryption and key rotation under our control.
[02:10] Maya: We support KMS/HSM integrations for dedicated and private deployments. For hosted, we offer customer-managed keys (CMK) via the major cloud providers; the keys can be rotated and Redwood logs key usage in audit trails.
[02:23] Tom: And audit logs — detail level? We need immutable logs for requests, but redacted so no PHI.
[02:29] Diego: We can emit request metadata (timestamps, latency, model version) to audit logs, and we can optionally include a redacted prompt hash for traceability. Full prompt text would only be stored if you opt in for debugging and the data is scrubbed.
[02:42] Aisha: So for the pilot we want: no persistent prompt storage, logs emitted to our Splunk with redacted prompts, and an acceptance test where 10,000 sample requests are run and logs are verified to contain no PII — is that feasible?
[02:54] Diego: Yes that's feasible. We'll provide the benchmark harness to run the 10k requests and a post-run log scrub report.
[03:00] Sara: About benchmarking — do you have tooling to measure token-level cost and throughput? We need to compare hosted vs dedicated to estimate unit economics.
[03:07] Diego: We do. Our harness measures tokens/sec, tokens per request, and also computes estimated cost under different config profiles (batching, quantization). For the POC we'll run both an optimized hosted profile and a dedicated small pool to show delta.
[03:19] Maya: Timeline check — if we start early next week: integration (3 days), baseline runs (2 days), tweak redaction and run acceptance (4 days) — total two weeks. Any blockers?
[03:30] Tom: Network — we may need VPC peering for dedicated or a private deployment. I'll need firewall rules and IP ranges.
[03:36] Maya: We'll send a networking checklist. Diego, can you prepare the IP ranges and expected ports?
[03:41] Diego: Yup, I'll include firewall/NAT details and sample peering config.
[03:45] [crosstalk] Aisha: One more — retention policy: we want logs kept for 90 days, prompts never stored. Can retention be configured per environment?
[03:53] Diego: Yeah retention is configurable at the tenant and route level. For hosted we can set retention to 0 days for prompt text and 90 days for metadata logs. For private/dedicated you control retention via your storage config.
[04:03] Sara: Any compliance docs we can review? SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports?
[04:07] Maya: We'll share SOC2 summary, recent pen test redacted report, and our data flow diagram. I'll put those in the follow-up email.
[04:15] Tom: For acceptance criteria, we'll define success as: (1) 10k run completes with p95 <= 800ms AND p50 <= 250ms, (2) no PII in logs (automated check), (3) exported metrics and cost estimates produced.
[04:27] Diego: Makes sense. A quick note on imperfections: for longer conversation flows and KV cache we may see variance, we should define the median prompt length for the test.
[04:35] Aisha: We'll provide a representative sample of short and long prompts; short ones ~25 tokens, long ~400 tokens.
[04:41] Maya: Ok great. Any other blockers?
[04:44] Sara: Not from product. Next steps recap?
[04:46] Maya: I'll send the security pack and SOC2, Diego will publish the benchmark harness and network checklist, Aisha you'll share sample payloads and flagged PII fields. We'll schedule Tom + Diego deep-dive for KMS and networking next week.
[04:58] Tom: Sounds good.
[05:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the thread and a calendar invite for the deep-dive. Bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: some speaker overlaps and small recognition errors (product names like "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash").
notes: Customer stressed PII removal and auditability. Agreed to two-week POC with 10k-run acceptance tests. Redwood to provide security docs, benchmark harness, and network checklist.
